title: Netting Unused Authorized Program Days on Work Conditioning and Work Hardening Extensions
content:
# Netting unused authorized program days

*Authorization desk questions and answers — Workers' Compensation Referral, Work Conditioning Program and Work Hardening Program.*

**What are the netted unused days?** The authorized program days that an extension request takes off because the authorization in force still has them. The netted unused days are the lesser of the authorized program days still unused and the calendar days left before the end date of the authorization in force where that end date falls zero to the program's extension lead days after the day of the request, none where that end date has already passed, and every authorized program day still unused otherwise.

**What is the program's extension lead time?** 3 calendar days in both the Work Conditioning Program and the Work Hardening Program.

**How are the days left counted?** In calendar days from the day of the request to the end date of the authorization in force; an end date falling on the day of the request is zero days left.

**What does each case net?**

| End date of the authorization in force | Netted unused days |
|---|---|
| already passed | none |
| 0 to 3 calendar days after the request | the lesser of the unused authorized days and the days left |
| more than 3 calendar days after the request | every unused authorized program day |

**Worked cases (hypothetical, 5 authorized program days unused, lead time of 3 days).**

| End date | Days left | Netted |
|---|---|---|
| 2 days before the request | passed | none |
| the day of the request | 0 | 0 |
| 2 days after the request | 2 | 2 |
| 3 days after the request | 3 | 3 |
| 4 days after the request | 4 | 5 — every unused day |
| 10 days after the request | 10 | 5 — every unused day |

**And with fewer unused days than days left?** With 1 unused day and an end date 3 days away, the lesser figure is 1.
